title: NSIC Rc 590 (Submarino 2) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 590 is an inbred rice for flood prone fields: about 144 days and 3.9 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 590 is an inbred rice variety for flood prone fields, known locally as Submarino 2. The NSIC approved it in 2020. It matures in about 144 days and averages 3.9 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 4.4 tonnes in trials.

heroImage.alt: A storm over rice paddies, the flood risk NSIC Rc 590 is bred to face

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 590, or Rc 590, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 3.9 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 78 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 4.4 tonnes.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.caption: Key facts of NSIC Rc 590 (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 590 yield?

On average it gives 3.9 tonnes per hectare. That is about 78 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits close to the average of the 1 inbred on the list, which is 3.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 4.4 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 144 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as long duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits fields that flood in the wet season. Even so, drain the field as soon as the water allows, because a long flood still costs yield. Our guide to [typhoon preparation](/blog/typhoon-preparation-for-farmers) helps you plan for storms. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 590?
items.a: It is known as Submarino 2. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 590 take to harvest?
items.a: About 144 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 590?
items.a: It averages 3.9 tonnes per hectare, about 78 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 4.4 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has low amylose, 16.2 percent. So it cooks soft.
